tagline: From nǐ hǎo to HSK mastery — tones, characters and all

help.intro: In Mandarin, pitch is part of the word: mā, má, mǎ and mà are four different words. Listen and copy the melody exactly — the tone matters as much as the letters.

tips.title: Tone gestures
tips.text: 1st = sing it flat and high (a doctor's "aaah"). 2nd = rising "huh?". 3rd = a low, skeptical dip ("we-ell…"). 4th = a sharp "No!". Say the gesture, and the tone follows.

tips.title: ⚠️ Tones are not optional (Z1)
tips.text: English uses pitch for attitude; Mandarin uses it for identity. 买 mǎi = buy, 卖 mài = sell — get the tone wrong and you say the opposite word.

phrases.translation: mā má mǎ mà — mother · hemp · horse · scold
1st tone (high & flat): mā gāo tiān sān
2nd tone (rising "huh?"): rén lái máng shéi
3rd tone (the low dip): mǎ hǎo wǒ nǐ
4th tone (sharp fall "No!"): mà shì qù dà
Neutral tone (the 2nd syllable relaxes): māma xièxie wǒmen
Māma mà mǎ. — Mum scolds the horse. (All one sound, mā-ma-mà-mǎ!)

help.intro: Pinyin uses the letters you know, but a few carry different sounds. Learn only where pinyin differs from English — the rest is free.

tips.title: ⚠️ Don't read pinyin as English (Z3)
tips.text: c = "ts" (cats), q = "ch" with a smile, x = soft "sh" with a smile, z = "ds" (kids), zh/ch/sh/r = tongue curled back. "Cài" is tsài, never "kai".

tips.title: b d g: a puff of air, not a voice (Z4)
tips.text: Mandarin b/d/g are gentle, unvoiced p/t/k; p/t/k add a strong puff of air. The contrast is the puff — bā vs pā.

phrases.translation: c = "ts": cài cǎo — vegetable, grass
q = "ch" + smile: qī qǐng qù — seven, please, go
x = soft "sh" + smile: xièxie xiǎo xī — thanks, small, west
zh/ch/sh = tongue curled back: Zhōngguó chī shì
r = a buzzy r, no lip rounding: rén rè Rìběn
z = "ds": zàijiàn zuò — goodbye, sit
b vs p — the puff of air: bàba pà — dad, fear
ü = say "ee", round your lips: nǚ lǜ qù — woman, green, go

quizzes.title: Pronouns 我 / 你 / 他 / 她

help.intro: The people words. Good news: they never change form — no "I/me/my" gymnastics. 们 turns people-words plural.

tips.title: The 们 plural
tips.text: 我 I → 我们 we; 你 you → 你们 you all; 他 he → 他们 they. 们 works on people only — nouns themselves have no plural at all (Z9).

tips.title: 他 and 她 sound the same
tips.text: Both are tā. In speech, gender comes for free — only writing distinguishes 他 (he) from 她 (she).

help.intro: 是 shì is "to be" between two nouns: 我是学生 — I am a student. It never changes form (no am/is/are!), and note: no "a/an" needed either.

tips.title: One form, forever
tips.text: 我是, 你是, 他是, 我们是 — all just 是. No conjugation exists in Chinese (Z9). Negate with 不: 我不是老师.

tips.title: ⚠️ 是 links NOUNS only (Z10 preview)
tips.text: She is tall = 她很高 — no 是! Adjectives work like verbs in Chinese. 是 + adjective (她是高 ✗) is the classic English-speaker error. The next module drills this.

help.intro: Learn ten characters and you can count to 99: eleven is "ten-one" (十一), twenty-two is "two-ten-two" (二十二). It's arithmetic, not memorization.

tips.title: Lego numbers
tips.text: 11 = 十一 (10+1), 20 = 二十 (2×10), 35 = 三十五 (3×10+5). Every number to 99 is built from 一 to 十 — compare English's eleven, twelve, twenty…

tips.title: ⚠️ 二 vs 两
tips.text: Counting uses 二 (èr): 一, 二, 三. But "two of something" uses 两 (liǎng): 两百 two hundred, and later 两个人 two people.

help.intro: Your first conversation — listen and repeat, copying the tones.

tips.title: Copy the melody, not just the sounds
tips.text: Shadow the voice: hum the pitch pattern first, then add the consonants and vowels. Tone is half the word (Z1).

help.intro: To ask a yes/no question, say the statement and add 吗 — nothing moves, nothing inverts. 呢 bounces a question back: 你呢? — and you?

tips.title: Statement + 吗 = question (Z12)
tips.text: 你是学生。You are a student. → 你是学生吗？Are you a student? No inversion, no "do" — Chinese questions leave the sentence untouched.

tips.title: 呢 = "and…?"
tips.text: 我很好，你呢？ I'm fine — and you? 呢 recycles the whole previous question in one syllable.

help.intro: The script stays hidden — listen first, then answer. Play it as often as you like.

tips.title: Catch the anchors
tips.text: Listen for 叫 (called), 是…人 (nationality) and 学生 (student) — those three anchors answer everything here.

help.intro: 叫 jiào = to be called (given name), 姓 xìng = to be surnamed. Nationality is country + 人: 中国人 = China-person.

tips.title: Country + 人 = nationality
tips.text: 中国 China → 中国人 Chinese. 英国 Britain → 英国人 British. One pattern, every nationality — no -ish/-ese/-an endings to memorize.

tips.title: Surname first
tips.text: Chinese names put the family name first: 王小美 is Ms. WANG Xiaomei. Teachers are Surname + 老师: 王老师.

quizzes.title: Tone pairs & the 你好 rule

help.intro: Real words come in tone pairs — and one pair changes: two 3rd tones in a row can't both dip, so the first one rises. 你好 is really ní hǎo.

tips.title: ⚠️ Two dips can't dance (Z2)
tips.text: 3rd + 3rd → 2nd + 3rd. 你好 nǐ hǎo → ní hǎo, 很好 hěn hǎo → hén hǎo. Pinyin still writes the original tones — your mouth makes the switch.

tips.title: Drill in pairs
tips.text: Words live as two-syllable teams. Practicing pairs (1+2, 2+4, 3+3…) trains your ear faster than single syllables.

help.intro: Characters aren't random pictures — they're built from parts. These eight parts (radicals) return inside hundreds of characters as meaning hints.

tips.title: ⚠️ Meaning left, sound right (Z7)
tips.text: About 80% of characters pair a meaning part with a sound part: 妈 mā = 女 (woman, the meaning) + 马 mǎ (the sound). Learn components, not strokes.

tips.title: Characters compose
tips.text: 好 (good) = 女 woman + 子 child. 明 (bright) = 日 sun + 月 moon. Every character you learn makes the next one cheaper.

tips.title: Type pinyin, pick the character

help.intro: 什么 = what, 谁 = who. The question word sits exactly where the answer will sit — nothing moves to the front.

tips.title: ⚠️ The question word stays put (Z12)
tips.text: English fronts "what": WHAT do you buy? Chinese keeps it in the answer's slot: 你买**什么**？(you buy WHAT?). Answer: 你买茶 — same shape.

tips.title: Swap-in trick
tips.text: Take the answer sentence and swap the unknown for 什么/谁: 她是我的老师 → 她是**谁**？

quizzes.title: Adjectives take 很, never 是

help.intro: To say "she is tall", Chinese drops "is" and glues the adjective on with 很: 她很高. Adjectives behave like verbs — they need no copula.

tips.title: 很 is the glue, not "very"
tips.text: Plain 她很高 just means "she's tall" — this 很 is nearly empty. To actually stress it, use 真 (really) or 非常 (extremely).

tips.title: ⚠️ 是 + adjective is the classic error (Z10)
tips.text: 她是高 ✗ — 是 links nouns only. And a bare 她高 sounds like a comparison ("SHE's the tall one"). Default shape: subject + 很 + adjective.

help.intro: Chinese family words are precise: older and younger siblings get different words. The doubled syllables (妈妈, 爸爸) are easy to say and hear.

tips.title: Older/younger is built in
tips.text: 哥哥 older brother vs 弟弟 younger brother; 姐姐 older sister vs 妹妹 younger sister. There is no plain word for just "brother".

tips.title: The neutral second syllable
tips.text: In 妈妈, 爸爸, 哥哥… the second syllable relaxes to a neutral tone: māma, bàba, gēge.

help.intro: 的 de is the possessive clip: 我的书 = my book, 老师的茶 = the teacher's tea. Close relationships and family often drop it: 我妈妈.

tips.title: Owner + 的 + thing (Z19)
tips.text: Whatever describes a noun comes BEFORE it, clipped on with 的. This little word later carries whole relative clauses — the habit starts here.

tips.title: Family drops 的
tips.text: 我妈妈 (my mum), 我家 (my home), 我朋友 (my friend) — with close people the 的 usually disappears.

quizzes.title: 有 + the measure word 个

help.intro: 有 yǒu = to have / there is. And counting anything needs a measure word between the number and the noun: 一**个**人, never 一人.

tips.title: ⚠️ Every noun brings its suitcase (Z11)
tips.text: Number (or 这/那) + MEASURE WORD + noun, always. 个 gè is the all-purpose suitcase — when in doubt, 个. English already does this with "a CUP of tea, a PAIR of trousers".

tips.title: 有 negates with 没 (Z18)
tips.text: 我有猫 I have a cat → 我**没**有猫 I don't. Never 不有 — 有 is the one verb that refuses 不.

help.intro: 这 zhè = this (near), 那 nà = that (far), 哪 nǎ = which (the question twin). Pointing at things needs the measure word too: 这个, 那本.

tips.title: nà = that, nǎ = which?

tips.title: 这/那 + MW + noun

help.intro: Listen to Xiaomei describe her family. Catch the counting word 口 and who does what.

tips.title: 口 counts family members
tips.text: Family size uses the measure word 口 (mouth): 五口人 = five mouths to feed. Anywhere else, people take 个.

help.intro: Two ways to ask "how many": 几 for small countable numbers (expects <10, needs a measure word), 多少 for anything (measure word optional).

tips.title: 几 + MW, 多少 free

tips.title: 几 also tells time
tips.text: 几点? = what time? (literally "how-many o'clock") — coming in the next module.

help.intro: Tom introduces his family. Notice 也 (also) sliding in before the verb: 我妈妈**也**是医生.

tips.title: 也 sits before the verb
tips.text: "Too/also" is 也, and it always lands in front of the verb: 她也是学生 — never at the end like English "too".

tips.title: ⚠️ Sandhi is automatic, pinyin isn't (Z2)
tips.text: Pinyin keeps writing nǐ hǎo with two dips — your mouth converts the first to a rise. Read pinyin with your ears, not your eyes.

tips.title: Keep the last dip low
tips.text: In a 3+3 pair only the FIRST syllable changes. The final third tone stays a low dip — don't lift it.

help.intro: 不 bù makes things negative and sits right before the verb or adjective: 我不忙 — I'm not busy. (Only 有 refuses it and takes 没.)

tips.title: 不 + verb/adjective
tips.text: 不是 is not, 不去 doesn't go, 不忙 not busy. One word, one slot — no "don't/doesn't/isn't" zoo (Z9).

tips.title: 不 changes tone before a 4th tone
tips.text: bù + 4th tone → bú: 不是 bú shì, 不累 bú lèi. Your ear probably does it already — now you know why.

tips.text: 红色**的**车 a red car, 大**的**桌子 the big table — description + 的 + noun, always in that order.

quizzes.title: Reading: 我的朋友小美

help.intro: Meet 小美, Tom's friend. Everything here uses this module's grammar: 很 + adjective, 的, 有/没有, and the measure words 个 and 只.

tips.title: 可是 = but
tips.text: The passage ends with 可是 (but) — your first sentence connector. 但是 is its slightly more formal twin.

quizzes.passage: 小美是我的好朋友。她是中国人，她家在北京。小美很高，也很好看。她有一个弟弟，他叫小明。小明很小，他不是学生。小美家有一只白色的猫。我很喜欢小美的猫，可是我没有猫。

Xiǎoměi shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou. Tā shì Zhōngguó rén, tā jiā zài Běijīng. Xiǎoměi hěn gāo, yě hěn hǎokàn. Tā yǒu yí ge dìdi, tā jiào Xiǎomíng. Xiǎomíng hěn xiǎo, tā bú shì xuésheng. Xiǎoměi jiā yǒu yì zhī báisè de māo. Wǒ hěn xǐhuan Xiǎoměi de māo, kěshì wǒ méiyǒu māo.

help.intro: Weekdays are numbered (星期一 = weekday-one = Monday), months are numbered (二月 = two-month = February). Two patterns replace fourteen English words.

tips.title: Count your week
tips.text: 星期一 Monday … 星期六 Saturday — then Sunday breaks the pattern: 星期天 (or 星期日), the "sky/sun day".

tips.title: Dates run big → small
tips.text: Year 年 → month 月 → day 号 → weekday: 2026年7月2号星期四. Chinese time always zooms from large to small.

help.intro: The word-order cliff: English says "I get up at seven"; Chinese sets the scene first — 我七点起床 (I at-seven get up). Time never trails the verb.

tips.title: ⚠️ Set the scene, then act (Z13)
tips.text: Subject + WHEN + (WHERE) + verb: 我明天去北京. Putting time at the end (我去北京明天 ✗) is the #1 English-speaker word-order error.

tips.title: Time can also lead
tips.text: For emphasis the time may open the sentence: 明天我去北京. Before the subject or after it — but never after the verb.

help.intro: Say your daily routine aloud — feel how the time expression always lands before the action.

tips.title: Chunk it: WHEN + DO
tips.text: Pause mentally after the time chunk: 我七点 // 起床. Building the habit aloud installs the word order for free (Z13).

help.intro: 在 zài marks where: 我在家 I'm at home. Doing something somewhere puts the 在-phrase BEFORE the verb: 我在家吃饭 — at home (I) eat.

tips.title: ⚠️ 在 + place + verb (Z13/Z29)
tips.text: 我在咖啡馆学习 — "I at the café study." English appends "at the café"; Chinese sets the scene before the action. 我学习在咖啡馆 ✗.

tips.title: 在 alone = to be at
tips.text: With no other verb, 在 IS the verb: 他在家 he's home, 你在哪儿? where are you?

help.intro: Listen for the times — they always come right before the action they schedule.

tips.title: Numbers first
tips.text: Catch 七点, 七点半, 八点, 十二点 — pin each time to the verb that follows it and the whole story falls into place.

help.intro: Verbs chain directly in Chinese: 去买咖啡 = go buy coffee. No "to", no linking word — the second verb is the purpose of the first.

tips.title: Verbs stack bare (Z29)
tips.text: 我去学校学习中文 — go + study, no connector. English needs "to"; Chinese just lines the actions up in order of happening.

quizzes.title: Can: 会 / 能 / 可以

help.intro: English "can" splits three ways: 会 = learned skill, 能 = physically/circumstantially able, 可以 = allowed.

tips.title: ⚠️ Skill 会, power 能, permission 可以 (Z26)
tips.text: Learned it? 会 (我会说中文). Able right now? 能 (今天我不能来). Allowed? 可以 (这儿可以坐吗?). Pick by asking WHY you "can".

tips.title: 会 also predicts
tips.text: Later, 会 marks likely futures: 明天会下雨 — it will rain. Skill first, forecast later.

quizzes.title: Reading: 汤姆的一天

help.intro: A full day, scheduled the Chinese way: every time and place stands before its verb. Read it twice — once for the story, once for the word order.

tips.title: Spot the pattern (Z13)
tips.text: Underline mentally: 七点起床, 在学校学习, 晚上六点回家 — WHEN/WHERE + verb, sentence after sentence. That rhythm is the grammar.

quizzes.passage: 汤姆每天早上七点起床，七点半喝咖啡。八点他去学校，在学校学习中文。十二点他和朋友吃午饭。下午他在图书馆看书。晚上六点他回家做饭。他会做英国菜，可是他更想学做中国菜。晚上他有时候看电视，有时候给妈妈打电话。他十一点睡觉。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng, qī diǎn bàn hē kāfēi. Bā diǎn tā qù xuéxiào, zài xuéxiào xuéxí Zhōngwén. Shí'èr diǎn tā hé péngyou chī wǔfàn. Xiàwǔ tā zài túshūguǎn kàn shū. Wǎnshang liù diǎn tā huí jiā zuòfàn. Tā huì zuò Yīngguó cài, kěshì tā gèng xiǎng xué zuò Zhōngguó cài. Wǎnshang tā yǒushíhou kàn diànshì, yǒushíhou gěi māma dǎ diànhuà. Tā shíyī diǎn shuìjiào.

Tom gets up at seven every morning and drinks coffee at 7:30. At eight he goes to school, where he studies Chinese. At twelve he eats lunch with friends. In the afternoon he reads in the library. At six in the evening he goes home and cooks. He can cook British food, but he'd rather learn to cook Chinese food. In the evening he sometimes watches TV, sometimes phones his mum. He goes to bed at eleven.

help.intro: Three sound contrasts English ears blur: the -n/-ng endings, the smiling j/q/x row, and ü. Exaggerate them now, relax later.

tips.title: ⚠️ fán ≠ fáng (Z5)
tips.text: -n ends with the tongue tip at the teeth; -ng ends open, in the throat. 半 bàn vs 帮 bāng, 人 rén vs 冷 lěng — different words.

tips.title: ü = "ee" with rounded lips
tips.text: Say "ee", freeze your tongue, round your lips: 去 qù, 女 nǚ, 绿 lǜ. After j/q/x it's written u but still sounds ü.

help.intro: Your first dialogue. Notice how the answer to a Chinese question keeps the question's exact shape — 能…吗? → 能!

tips.title: Answer with the verb

help.intro: Verb + 了 stamps an action as completed: 我买了一本书 — I bought a book. It's a ✓-stamp, not a past tense: habits and states never take it.

tips.title: A ✓-stamp, not a tense (Z14)
tips.text: Ask "did the action complete?" — if yes, stamp the verb: 吃了, 买了, 去了. If you're describing a habit or a state, no stamp.

tips.title: ⚠️ Past ≠ 了
tips.text: 昨天我很忙 (yesterday I was busy) has NO 了 — 忙 is a state, nothing completed. 每天…了 ✗ too: habits aren't single completed events. This is the #1 error at every level.

help.intro: Beyond 个: nouns sort by shape and kind. 本 for bound things, 张 for flat things, 条 for long bendy things, 只 for animals, 杯 cups, 瓶 bottles, 件 clothes-tops, 双 pairs, 辆 vehicles, 位 people (polite).

tips.title: English does this too
tips.text: A PAIR of trousers, a SHEET of paper, a CUP of tea — English partitives are measure words in disguise. Chinese just applies them to every noun.

quizzes.title: Sounds: 不 & 一 change tone

help.intro: Two everyday words bend their tone: 不 bù → bú before a 4th tone, and 一 yī → yí before a 4th, yì before the rest. Say them until it's automatic.

tips.title: ⚠️ 不 flips before a fall (Z2)
tips.text: bù + 4th → bú: 不是 bú shì, 不去 bú qù, 不累 bú lèi. Everywhere else it stays bù: 不高, 不忙, 不喝.

tips.title: 一 has three faces
tips.text: Counting: yī (一, 十一). Before a 4th tone: yí (一件, 一个*). Before tones 1/2/3: yì (一杯, 一瓶, 一本). *个 counts as 4th.

tips.title: ⚠️ Verb + landing (Z21)
tips.text: English packs result into the verb (find, hear); Chinese splits it: 找 look + 到 = find; 听 listen + 懂 = understand (by ear); 吃 eat + 完 = finish eating.

tips.title: The landing takes the 了
tips.text: 我看完了这本书 — the ✓-stamp follows the whole verb+landing unit: 看完了, 找到了, 听懂了.

help.intro: 来 = toward me, 去 = away from me. Glued after motion verbs they give English's "in/out/up/back": 进来 come in, 出去 go out, 回来 come back.

tips.title: The speaker is the compass (Z21)
tips.text: Every direction is measured from where YOU stand: 上来 up (toward me), 上去 up (away). Change where you stand and 来/去 swap.

tips.title: Places squeeze in the middle
tips.text: With a place, it slots before 来/去: 回家去, 进教室来 — never after: 回去家 ✗.

quizzes.title: Reading: 学中文的路

help.intro: Tom's first year — told with this module's whole toolkit: duration, landings, the three de, and one tone slip that proves why tones matter.

tips.title: ⚠️ wèn ≠ wěn
tips.text: 问 (ask, 4th tone) vs 吻 (kiss, 3rd tone) — the passage's joke is a real cautionary tale about tones (Z1).

quizzes.passage: 汤姆学中文学了一年了。开始的时候，他觉得声调太难了，常常说错。有一次，他想说"我想问你"，可是说成了"我想吻你"，大家都笑了。现在他听得懂老师说的话，也看得懂简单的中文书。他每天认真地学习，写字写得越来越漂亮。王老师说："学外语就是这样：慢慢来，别怕说错。"汤姆觉得，虽然中文很难，但是他学得很开心。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le. Kāishǐ de shíhou, tā juéde shēngdiào tài nán le, chángcháng shuō cuò. Yǒu yí cì, tā xiǎng shuō "wǒ xiǎng wèn nǐ", kěshì shuō chéng le "wǒ xiǎng wěn nǐ", dàjiā dōu xiào le. Xiànzài tā tīng de dǒng lǎoshī shuō de huà, yě kàn de dǒng jiǎndān de Zhōngwén shū. Tā měitiān rènzhēn de xuéxí, xiě zì xiě de yuèláiyuè piàoliang. Wáng lǎoshī shuō: "Xué wàiyǔ jiù shì zhèyàng: mànmàn lái, bié pà shuō cuò." Tāngmǔ juéde, suīrán Zhōngwén hěn nán, dànshì tā xué de hěn kāixīn.

Tom has been learning Chinese for a year now. At the beginning he found the tones too hard and often misspoke. Once he meant to say "I want to ask you" (wèn) but said "I want to kiss you" (wěn) — everyone laughed. Now he can understand what the teacher says and read simple Chinese books. He studies conscientiously every day, and his characters look better and better. Teacher Wang says: "That's what learning a language is: take it slowly, don't fear mistakes." Tom feels that although Chinese is hard, he's learning it very happily.

quizzes.title: Listening: 王老师的建议

help.intro: Teacher Wang's three tips — a listening full of landings (学好, 说错, 写完, 写对) and both de-graders.

tips.title: 第 makes ordinals
tips.text: 第一, 第二, 第三 — first, second, third. 第 + number turns any count into a ranking.

quizzes.passage: 很多学生问我，怎么才能学好中文。我想说三件事。第一，每天都要听，听得越多，懂得越多。第二，别怕说错。说错了没关系，说得多了，就说得好了。第三，认真地写汉字。写完一个字，要问自己：我写对了吗？因为学外语不容易，所以要慢慢来。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Hěn duō xuésheng wèn wǒ, zěnme cái néng xué hǎo Zhōngwén. Wǒ xiǎng shuō sān jiàn shì. Dì yī, měitiān dōu yào tīng, tīng de yuè duō, dǒng de yuè duō. Dì èr, bié pà shuō cuò. Shuō cuò le méi guānxi, shuō de duō le, jiù shuō de hǎo le. Dì sān, rènzhēn de xiě Hànzì. Xiě wán yí ge zì, yào wèn zìjǐ: wǒ xiě duì le ma? Yīnwèi xué wàiyǔ bù róngyì, suǒyǐ yào mànmàn lái.

Many students ask me how to master Chinese. I'd say three things. First, listen every day — the more you hear, the more you understand. Second, don't fear mistakes. Misspeaking doesn't matter: speak a lot and you'll speak well. Third, write characters carefully. When you finish one, ask yourself: did I write it right? Learning a language isn't easy, so take it step by step.

help.intro: The whole module in a story: durations (两天, 十二个小时), landings (买来), pairs (因为…所以) and a graded 得 (好得这么快).

tips.title: 买来 = bought & brought

quizzes.passage: 上个星期，汤姆病了。他头疼，肚子也疼，两天没去上课。小美给他买来了药和水果。她说："多休息，多喝水，你很快就会好的。"汤姆吃了药，睡了十二个小时。第二天，他觉得好多了。他给小美打电话："谢谢你！因为你的帮助，所以我好得这么快。"小美笑着说："别客气！朋友就是要互相帮助。"
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Shàng ge xīngqī, Tāngmǔ bìng le. Tā tóu téng, dùzi yě téng, liǎng tiān méi qù shàngkè. Xiǎoměi gěi tā mǎi lái le yào hé shuǐguǒ. Tā shuō: "Duō xiūxi, duō hē shuǐ, nǐ hěn kuài jiù huì hǎo de." Tāngmǔ chī le yào, shuì le shí'èr ge xiǎoshí. Dì èr tiān, tā juéde hǎo duō le. Tā gěi Xiǎoměi dǎ diànhuà: "Xièxie nǐ! Yīnwèi nǐ de bāngzhù, suǒyǐ wǒ hǎo de zhème kuài." Xiǎoměi xiào zhe shuō: "Bié kèqi! Péngyou jiù shì yào hùxiāng bāngzhù."

Last week Tom fell ill. His head hurt, his stomach too, and he missed class for two days. Xiaomei bought him medicine and fruit. She said: "Rest a lot, drink lots of water — you'll be better in no time." Tom took the medicine and slept twelve hours. The next day he felt much better. He phoned Xiaomei: "Thank you! It's thanks to your help that I got better so fast." Xiaomei said with a smile: "Don't mention it! Friends are there to help each other."

tips.text: Say the description as one breath and land on the noun: 穿红衣服的//那个人. The noun is the finish line (Z19).

help.intro: For past events, 是…的 spotlights when/where/how: 我是昨天来的 — it was YESTERDAY that I came. The event is known; the detail is the news.

tips.title: ⚠️ Known event, new detail (Z28)
tips.text: Use 是…的 when the happening is old news and you're asking or telling the circumstance: 你是怎么来的? (HOW did you come?) — not plain 了, which reports the event itself.

tips.title: The frame
tips.text: 是 + [spotlighted detail + verb] + 的: 她是在北京学的中文, 我们是坐飞机来的.

help.intro: 如果 A，B 就… — if A, then B. The 就 sits inside the second clause, right before its verb: 如果下雨，我们就不去.

tips.title: Another pair to keep (Z25)
tips.text: 如果 opens the condition, 就 answers it. 就 is an adverb: it must stand before the verb, never before the subject — 就我们不去 ✗.

tips.title: No tense gymnastics
tips.text: English shifts tenses ("if it rains… we would…"); Chinese conditions stay bare: 如果…就 handles real and hypothetical alike (Z9).

quizzes.title: Reading: 我认识的人

help.intro: Four people, each introduced by a 的-clause. Parse each: find the 的, find the noun, then read the description before it.

tips.title: Chunk, don't crawl (Z8)
tips.text: 住在他楼上的|老爷爷 — split at the 的. Reading Chinese means grouping characters into words and clauses; the 的 is your best seam.

quizzes.passage: 在北京，汤姆认识了很多有意思的人。住在他楼上的老爷爷每天早上在公园里打太极拳，他是三十年前从上海来的。在咖啡馆工作的那个女孩儿会说四种语言，她说得又快又好。教汤姆写汉字的王老师写的字漂亮得像画儿一样。汤姆觉得，认识的人越多，他的中文就越好，生活也越来越有意思。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Zài Běijīng, Tāngmǔ rènshi le hěn duō yǒuyìsi de rén. Zhù zài tā lóushàng de lǎo yéye měitiān zǎoshang zài gōngyuán li dǎ tàijíquán, tā shì sānshí nián qián cóng Shànghǎi lái de. Zài kāfēiguǎn gōngzuò de nà ge nǚháir huì shuō sì zhǒng yǔyán, tā shuō de yòu kuài yòu hǎo. Jiāo Tāngmǔ xiě Hànzì de Wáng lǎoshī xiě de zì piàoliang de xiàng huàr yíyàng. Tāngmǔ juéde, rènshi de rén yuè duō, tā de Zhōngwén jiù yuè hǎo, shēnghuó yě yuèláiyuè yǒuyìsi.

In Beijing, Tom has gotten to know many interesting people. The old grandpa who lives upstairs does tai chi in the park every morning — he came from Shanghai thirty years ago. The girl who works at the café speaks four languages, fast and well. Teacher Wang, who teaches Tom to write characters, writes characters as beautiful as paintings. Tom finds that the more people he knows, the better his Chinese gets — and life keeps getting more interesting.

quizzes.title: Listening: 天气预报

help.intro: A weather forecast for four cities. Listen for city + weather + temperature — and one 比-comparison.

tips.title: 度 = degrees, 零下 = below zero
tips.text: 二十八度 28°, 零下十度 −10°. The 比-line: 比今天热三度 — hotter than today BY three degrees (the amount follows the adjective, Z24).

quizzes.passage: 大家好，现在播报明天的天气。北京明天是晴天，不刮风，白天二十八度，是个又暖和又舒服的日子。上海明天上午有小雨，下午雨就停了，二十五度。广州明天天气很热，三十四度，比今天热三度。哈尔滨的朋友要注意：明天下大雪，零下十度，出门的时候要多穿衣服。

Dàjiā hǎo, xiànzài bōbào míngtiān de tiānqì. Běijīng míngtiān shì qíngtiān, bù guā fēng, báitiān èrshíbā dù, shì ge yòu nuǎnhuo yòu shūfu de rìzi. quizzes.title: Reading: 北京的四季

help.intro: Four seasons, packed with this module's frames: 又…又, 越来越, 的-clauses and a closing 如果…就.

tips.title: 最 = the most
tips.text: 最热 hottest, 最漂亮 most beautiful, 最喜欢 favourite — 最 simply fronts the adjective. No "-est" forms to build.

quizzes.passage: 北京的四季很不一样。春天暖和，可是常常刮风。夏天又热又长，最热的时候有三十八度，白天出门的人都走得很快，因为大家都想快点儿回到凉快的家里。秋天是北京最漂亮的季节：天很蓝，路两边的树越来越黄，来公园拍照片的人也越来越多。冬天很冷，有时候下大雪。下雪的时候，孩子们玩得最高兴。汤姆最喜欢的季节是秋天。他说："如果你秋天来北京，就会爱上这个城市。"
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Běijīng de sìjì hěn bù yíyàng. Chūntiān nuǎnhuo, kěshì chángcháng guā fēng. Xiàtiān yòu rè yòu cháng, zuì rè de shíhou yǒu sānshíbā dù, báitiān chūmén de rén dōu zǒu de hěn kuài, yīnwèi dàjiā dōu xiǎng kuài diǎnr huí dào liángkuai de jiā li. Qiūtiān shì Běijīng zuì piàoliang de jìjié: tiān hěn lán, lù liǎngbiān de shù yuèláiyuè huáng, lái gōngyuán pāi zhàopiàn de rén yě yuèláiyuè duō. Dōngtiān hěn lěng, yǒushíhou xià dà xuě. Xià xuě de shíhou, háizimen wán de zuì gāoxìng. Tāngmǔ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié shì qiūtiān. Tā shuō: "Rúguǒ nǐ qiūtiān lái Běijīng, jiù huì àishàng zhè ge chéngshì."

Beijing's four seasons are very different. Spring is warm but often windy. Summer is hot and long — at its hottest it reaches 38 degrees, and people out in the daytime walk fast, because everyone wants to get back to a cool home. Autumn is Beijing's most beautiful season: the sky is blue, the trees along the roads turn more and more yellow, and more and more people come to the parks to take photos. Winter is cold, sometimes with heavy snow. When it snows, the children have the best time. Tom's favourite season is autumn. He says: "If you come to Beijing in autumn, you'll fall in love with this city."

tips.title: When to reach for 把

quizzes.title: Reading: 搬家

help.intro: Moving day: instructions with 把, one 被 for flavour, and comparisons between old home and new.

tips.title: 离 = distance from (Z29)
tips.text: 新家离学校更近 — 离 measures the gap between two places: A 离 B 近/远. It's a coverb: it stands before what it relates to.

quizzes.passage:
这个周末汤姆搬家了。新家比旧家大得多，离学校也更近。
小美和几个朋友都来帮忙。汤姆让大家先把大东西搬上车：床、桌子、椅子，还有那个最重的书柜。

"Where do we put the bookcase?" Xiaomei asked.
"Next to the window," said Tom. "Put the books in the bookcase and the clothes on the bed — I'll sort them out myself later."

quizzes.passage:
在中国生活了一年以后，汤姆觉得最方便的就是快递。你在手机上买的东西，第二天就能被送到家门口。快递员每天把成千上万个包裹送到城市的每一个角落，比很多国家的快递快得多，也便宜得多。
上个星期，汤姆把一本书寄给在上海的朋友。他早上把书交给快递员，朋友第二天中午就收到了。朋友给他发消息："收到了！这也太快了吧！"

After a year of living in China, Tom thinks the most convenient thing of all is the express delivery system. Something you buy on your phone can be delivered to your door the next day. Couriers deliver tens of thousands of parcels to every corner of the city every day — much faster and much cheaper than in many countries.
Last week, Tom mailed a book to a friend in Shanghai. He handed the book to the courier in the morning, and his friend received it the next day at noon. The friend messaged him: "Got it! That's just too fast!"
But delivery brings new problems too: people buy more and more, and packaging waste keeps growing. Many companies now have customers leave the boxes with the courier, so the boxes can be used again.

tips.title: 听起来 = it sounds…

quizzes.passage:
大家好，欢迎收听我们的播客。今天聊一个话题：好习惯是怎么来的？
很多人觉得，只要下定决心，就能改变自己。可是研究发现，只有把新习惯变得很小、很容易，才能坚持下去。比如，你想每天看书，就先从每天看一页开始。即使那天再忙，一页书也看得完。
还有一个方法：把新习惯放在老习惯后面。每天喝着咖啡的时候背五个生词——咖啡喝完了，生词也背完了。听起来很简单吧？无论你想养成什么习惯，都可以试试这个办法。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Hello everyone, welcome to our podcast. Today's topic: where do good habits come from?
Many people think that as long as you're determined, you can change yourself. But research finds that only by making a new habit small and easy can you keep it going. Say you want to read every day — start with one page a day. Even on your busiest day, one page is doable.
Another method: attach the new habit to an old one. Memorize five new words while drinking your daily coffee — when the coffee's finished, so are the words. Sounds simple, right? Whatever habit you want to build, give this method a try.

Xiaomei says: "Only by putting the phones down can we truly be together." So they made a deal: at dinner, whoever reaches for their phone first pays the bill. It sounds simple, but it works — even the most phone-addicted friend has stuck to it.

quizzes.title: Listening: 讲座 — 城市化

help.intro: A university-style lecture: the formal register in action — 使, 由于, 对于, 关于, 令人, 既…也.

tips.title: 既…也 = both…and (formal)
tips.text: 既带来了机会，也带来了挑战 — the written cousin of 又…又, joining two verb phrases in balanced style (Z30).

quizzes.passage:
各位同学，下午好。今天我们谈谈城市化。
过去四十年，中国经历了世界上规模最大的城市化：几亿人从农村搬进了城市。城市化使经济快速发展，也使几亿人的生活水平得到了很大的提高。
但是，对于城市化，我们不能只看到好的一面。由于人口增长太快，一些大城市出现了交通拥堵、住房紧张等问题。另外，很多年轻人进城工作，农村只留下了老人和孩子，这也是一个令人担心的社会问题。
总的来说，城市化既带来了机会，也带来了挑战。关于怎么解决这些问题，我们下节课继续讨论。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Good afternoon, everyone. Today let's talk about urbanization.
Over the past forty years, China has gone through the largest urbanization in the world: hundreds of millions of people moved from the countryside into cities. Urbanization made the economy grow fast and greatly raised the living standards of hundreds of millions.
But we can't see only the good side. Because the population grew too fast, some big cities developed problems like traffic congestion and housing shortages. Also, with young people leaving for city jobs, only the old and the young remain in the villages — a worrying social problem.
All in all, urbanization brings both opportunities and challenges. As for how to solve these problems — we'll continue next class.

quizzes.title: Reading: 科技与生活

help.intro: An HSK-5-style essay: balanced argument, formal frames (使, 对于, 由于, 关于, 则, 反而), and a quotable conclusion.

tips.title: 反而 = contrary to expectation
tips.text: 老人…反而被挡在门外 — instead (of being helped), they're shut out. 反而 flags an outcome that flips what the setup promised.

quizzes.passage:
过去十年，科技使我们的生活发生了巨大的变化。移动支付让钱包成为历史；网上购物使人们足不出户就能买到世界各地的商品；人工智能则开始进入医院、学校和家庭。
对于这些变化，人们的态度并不相同。支持者认为，科技提高了效率，使更多人享受到了方便的服务。由于看病可以网上挂号，农村的病人再也不用半夜排队了。
但也有人担心：老人学不会用智能手机，反而被新技术挡在了门外；年轻人越来越依赖手机，面对面的交流却越来越少。
关于科技，也许最重要的问题不是"它能做什么"，而是"我们想让它为我们做什么"。技术本身没有好坏，使用它的方式才决定它的价值。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Over the past decade, technology has transformed our lives. Mobile payment made wallets history; online shopping lets people buy goods from all over the world without leaving home; and artificial intelligence is entering hospitals, schools and homes.
Attitudes toward these changes differ. Supporters argue technology raises efficiency and brings convenient services to more people. Since hospital registration works online now, rural patients no longer queue at midnight.
But others worry: elderly people who can't master smartphones end up shut out by the new technology, and the young grow ever more dependent on their phones while face-to-face conversation shrinks.
Perhaps the most important question about technology is not "what can it do" but "what do we want it to do for us". Technology itself is neither good nor bad — how we use it decides its value.

help.intro: An interview in educated, natural register — 越…越, 造成, 既然, and the rhetoric of advice.

quizzes.passage:
记者："李老师，您做环保工作二十年了。在您看来，最大的变化是什么？"
李老师："最大的变化是人们的态度。二十年前，很多人觉得环保跟自己没关系。现在，垃圾分类、少用塑料袋，已经成了很多家庭的习惯。"
记者："那么，最让您担心的问题是什么？"
李老师："是速度。经济发展得越快，对环境的压力就越大。如果我们只顾眼前的利益，就会给下一代造成无法挽回的损失。"
记者："对于普通人，您有什么建议？"
李老师："从小事做起。既然改变世界很难，那就先改变自己的生活方式。"

Reporter: "Teacher Li, you've worked in environmental protection for twenty years. In your view, what's the biggest change?"
Li: "The biggest change is people's attitude. Twenty years ago, many felt the environment had nothing to do with them. Now sorting waste and cutting plastic bags are habits in many households."
Reporter: "And what worries you most?"
Li: "Speed. The faster the economy grows, the greater the pressure on the environment. If we only mind immediate gains, we'll cause the next generation irreversible losses."
Reporter: "Any advice for ordinary people?"
Li: "Start small. Since changing the world is hard, first change your own way of living."

help.intro: A model argumentative essay: thesis, two supports, a concession, a turn — with 成语, 由于, 往往 and 反而 doing the heavy lifting.

tips.title: 欲速则不达
tips.text: "Desire speed, and you won't arrive" — a classical 成语 quoted mid-essay, exactly how educated prose deploys them (Z30).

quizzes.passage:
在这个一切都追求"快"的时代，"慢"几乎成了一个贬义词。吃饭要快，走路要快，连休息都要"高效率"。然而，快真的总是好的吗？
首先，快容易使人马马虎虎。为了赶时间，我们常常把工作做得又快又糟，最后不得不花更多的时间去改正错误——欲速则不达，古人早就明白这个道理。
其次，快使我们失去了很多东西。由于急着赶路，我们看不见路边的风景；由于急着回消息，我们听不完朋友的一句话。生活的意义，往往就藏在这些被我们跳过的细节里。
当然，慢不等于懒。该快的时候快，该慢的时候慢，这才是真正的生活智慧。在人人都跑的时代，敢于慢下来，反而需要更大的勇气。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
In an era that chases "fast" in everything, "slow" has almost become a dirty word. Eat fast, walk fast — even rest must be "efficient". But is fast really always good?
First, speed breeds carelessness. Racing the clock, we do our work fast and badly, then spend more time fixing the mistakes — "haste brings no arrival," as the ancients already knew.
Second, speed costs us things. Rushing down the road, we miss the scenery beside it; rushing to answer messages, we don't hear a friend finish a sentence. Life's meaning often hides in exactly the details we skip.
Of course, slow is not lazy. Fast when it should be fast, slow when it should be slow — that is real wisdom about living. In an age when everyone runs, daring to slow down takes the greater courage.

quizzes.passageTitle: 社论：让城市为行人留一条路
quizzes.passage:
近年来，本市机动车数量持续增长，人行道却越修越窄，部分路段甚至被停放的车辆完全占用。行人被迫走上机动车道，安全问题日益突出。
有人认为，城市的首要任务是保证交通效率，行人应当"让路"。然而，这种观点岂不是本末倒置？城市因人而生，为人而建。一座只方便汽车而不方便行人的城市，谈何宜居？
因此，我们呼吁：第一，有关部门应尽快清理被占用的人行道，违规停车行为必须受到处罚；第二，新建道路必须为行人和自行车留出足够的空间；此外，学校、医院周边路段应设置更多的过街设施。
总之，衡量一座城市的文明程度，不在于它的高楼有多高，而在于它对最普通的行人有多友好。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Editorial: Leave the pedestrians a path
In recent years, the number of motor vehicles in our city has kept growing while pavements are built ever narrower — some stretches are entirely occupied by parked cars. Pedestrians are forced onto the roadway, and safety problems grow by the day.
Some argue a city's first task is traffic efficiency, and pedestrians should "give way". But isn't that putting the cart before the horse? Cities exist because of people and are built for people. A city convenient for cars but not for walkers — how could it be called livable?
We therefore urge: first, the authorities should promptly clear the occupied pavements, and illegal parking must be punished; second, new roads must reserve adequate space for pedestrians and bicycles; furthermore, more crossings should be installed near schools and hospitals.
In short, a city's civilization is measured not by the height of its towers but by its friendliness to the ordinary person on foot.

quizzes.passage:
关于图书馆使用情况的报告

本学期，图书馆的使用情况有了明显改善。与去年相比，每日到馆人数增长了三分之一。其中，周末的阅览室最受学生欢迎，常常座无虚席。
调查显示，大部分学生对新的开放时间表示满意，然而，也有部分同学建议，考试期间应将开放时间延长至晚上十一点。此外，自习区的座位仍然不足，高峰时段约有五分之一的学生找不到座位。
因此，我们建议：第一，增设两百个自习座位；第二，考试期间延长开放时间；第三，所有新措施均于下月起实行。

Report on library usage

This semester, library usage has clearly improved. Compared with last year, daily visits grew by one third. The weekend reading rooms are the most popular with students — often not an empty seat.
Surveys show most students are satisfied with the new opening hours; however, some suggest extending opening to 11 p.m. during exams. Furthermore, study-area seats remain insufficient: at peak times about one fifth of students cannot find a seat.
We therefore recommend: first, adding 200 study seats; second, longer hours during exams; third, all new measures to take effect from next month.

quizzes.passage:
如今流行一种全新的旅游方式，我称之为"打卡式"旅游。其要领如下：到达景点后，第一时间找到最佳拍照角度，拍照三十张，修图十分钟，发朋友圈一条，然后——奔赴下一个景点。至于景点本身？看没看，重要吗？
这种旅游效率之高，令人叹为观止。有人一天"游"了八个景点，晚上数着朋友圈的点赞，满意地宣布：这个城市，我玩明白了。古人说"读万卷书，行万里路"；今人则是"拍万张照，修万张图"。
当然，我并非反对拍照。只是，当我们连一分钟都不肯留给风景本身，当点赞数成了旅行唯一的"成果"，我们与其说是在看世界，不如说是在让世界看我们——看我们忙着看手机。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
On "check-in" tourism
A brand-new style of travel is in fashion; I call it "check-in" tourism. The technique: on arriving at a sight, immediately locate the best photo angle, take thirty shots, retouch for ten minutes, post one WeChat update — then dash to the next sight. As for the sight itself? Seen or not — does it matter?
The efficiency is breathtaking. Some "tour" eight sights in a day, count their likes at night, and declare with satisfaction: this city — nailed it. The ancients said, "Read ten thousand books, travel ten thousand miles"; our contemporaries: "Take ten thousand photos, retouch ten thousand pictures."
I'm not against photography, of course. But when we won't spare the scenery even one minute, when likes become a journey's only "achievement" — we are not so much seeing the world as letting the world watch us… watching our phones.

quizzes.passage:
在我的记忆里，家乡的秋天是有味道的。
是院子里桂花的甜香，混着新收的稻谷味儿；是母亲晒在竹竿上的辣椒，红得晃眼，辣得呛人。
那时候，日子过得慢。邮递员的自行车铃一响，半条街的人都探出头来；一封信，要读三遍：自己读一遍，念给奶奶听一遍，晚上躺在床上，在心里再读一遍。
如今我住在城里，秋天来了，只是手机上的一条消息："今日立秋。"我常想，我们得到了整个世界的消息，却弄丢了自己院子里的桂花香。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Reading: "Autumn in My Hometown" (prose excerpt)
In my memory, autumn in my hometown had a smell. It was the sweet scent of osmanthus in the courtyard mixed with newly harvested rice; it was the chilies my mother dried on bamboo poles — dazzling red, chokingly hot.
Days passed slowly then. When the postman's bicycle bell rang, half the street leaned out. A letter got read three times: once to yourself, once aloud to grandma, and once more at night, lying in bed, in your heart.
Now I live in the city, and autumn arrives as a phone notification: "Autumn begins today." I often think: we have gained the whole world's news, and lost the scent of osmanthus in our own courtyard.

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇书评

help.intro: A book review with a personality: ironic opener, concrete praise, an honest flaw, and 成语 (瑕不掩瑜, 大同小异) earning their keep.

tips.title: 瑕不掩瑜
tips.text: "The flaw doesn't hide the jade's luster" — THE set phrase for balanced reviews: acknowledge the defect, keep the praise (Z30).

quizzes.passageTitle: 书评：《深夜食堂里的中国》
quizzes.passage:
这本书的书名起得极好，好到让人担心内容配不上它。读完之后可以放心了：担心是多余的——内容比书名还好。
作者花了五年时间，走访了三十个城市的夜宵摊。他写烤串，写馄饨，写凌晨三点的一碗热汤面，但归根结底，他写的是人：下了夜班的护士，刚吵完架的小两口，把一天的委屈就着啤酒咽下去的中年人。文字平实，却处处见功夫——没有一个字在炫技，也没有一个字是多余的。
当然，书也并非无可挑剔。后三分之一略显重复，几个城市的故事读起来大同小异。但瑕不掩瑜：在人人都写"大时代"的今天，有人愿意蹲下来，认认真真地写一碗面，这本身就值得敬佩。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Book review: "China at the Midnight Diner"
The title is so good you worry the book can't live up to it. Having finished it, you can relax: the worry was superfluous — the book is better than its title.
The author spent five years visiting late-night food stalls in thirty cities. He writes skewers, wontons, a bowl of hot noodle soup at 3 a.m. — but in the end he writes people: the nurse coming off a night shift, the young couple fresh from a quarrel, the middle-aged man washing the day's grievances down with beer. The prose is plain yet masterful everywhere — not one character shows off, and not one is wasted.
The book isn't beyond criticism, of course. The final third feels repetitive; several cities' stories read much the same. But the flaw doesn't obscure the jade: in an age when everyone writes "the great era", someone willing to crouch down and write one bowl of noodles with full seriousness deserves respect in itself.

help.intro: A formal debate — 有目共睹, 与其…不如, 不但不…反而, and a rhetorical question as the knockout blow. Track each side's moves.

tips.title: 对方辩友
tips.text: "Our esteemed opponents" — the fixed courtesy address of Chinese debate. Attack the argument, honor the person (Z30).

quizzes.passageTitle: 辩论：人工智能会取代翻译吗？
quizzes.passage:
主持人："今天的辩题是：人工智能会不会取代人类翻译？请正方发言。"
正方："谢谢主持人。机器翻译的进步有目共睹：速度快、成本低、错误率逐年下降。日常翻译的大部分工作，机器已经可以胜任。与其否认现实，不如承认：这个行业正在被重新定义。"
反方："对方辩友只看到了效率，却忽略了语言的本质。翻译不是简单的词语转换，而是文化之间的桥梁。机器可以翻译"再见"，但它翻译得出"长亭外，古道边"里的离愁吗？在文学、外交这些领域，人类翻译不但不会被取代，反而会因为机器的存在而变得更加珍贵。"
主持人："双方观点都很精彩。看来问题的关键，不在于机器能做什么，而在于我们把什么交给机器。"
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Debate: Will AI replace human translators?
Host: "Today's motion: will artificial intelligence replace human translators? The affirmative side, please."
Affirmative: "Thank you. Machine translation's progress is plain to see: fast, cheap, with error rates falling year by year. Machines can already handle most everyday translation. Rather than deny reality, better to admit it: this industry is being redefined."
Negative: "Our opponents see only efficiency and ignore the nature of language. Translation is not word-swapping but a bridge between cultures. A machine can translate 'goodbye' — but can it translate the parting sorrow in a classical verse? In literature and diplomacy, human translators will not be replaced; the machine's existence will make them more precious."
Host: "Both sides excellent. It seems the key is not what machines can do, but what we choose to hand them."

quizzes.title: Reading: 一篇新闻分析

help.intro: Journalistic analysis at full register: 表面上…实际上, 换言之, 综上所述, a porcelain metaphor, and a wordplay ending. Read for the argument's architecture.

tips.title: The pivot: 表面上…实际上
tips.text: "On the surface… in reality" — the analysis genre's signature move: open with the visible dispute, pivot to the structural one (Z30).

quizzes.passageTitle: 新闻分析：预制菜进校园之争
quizzes.passage:
近日，多地家长对"预制菜进校园"表达担忧，相关话题连续数日占据热搜。表面上看，这是一场关于食品安全的争论；实际上，它触及的是一个更深层的问题：公共决策中的信任。
预制菜本身并非洪水猛兽。业内人士指出，规范生产的预制菜，其安全标准未必低于现场烹饪。然而，家长的愤怒并非毫无来由——真正令他们不安的，是"不知情"：孩子每天吃什么，竟需要通过网络爆料才能得知。
换言之，问题的核心不是"能不能吃"，而是"谁来决定、谁被告知"。有关部门若只强调检测合格，而回避决策程序的透明，恐怕难以真正平息质疑。信任如同瓷器，打碎容易，修复极难。
综上所述，与其在舆论发酵后被动回应，不如在决策之初就把家长请到桌前。毕竟，公共信任才是最经不起"预制"的东西。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
News analysis: the school pre-made meals controversy
Recently, parents in many cities voiced concern over "pre-made meals entering school canteens", and the topic dominated trending lists for days. On the surface it is a food-safety debate; in fact it touches something deeper: trust in public decision-making.
Pre-made meals are no monster in themselves. Industry insiders note that properly produced ones may meet safety standards no lower than on-site cooking. Yet the parents' anger is not groundless — what truly unsettles them is not knowing: they learned what their children eat daily only through online exposés.
In other words, the core issue is not "is it safe to eat" but "who decides, and who gets told". If the authorities stress only that tests were passed while avoiding transparency about the decision-making process, the doubts will hardly subside. Trust is like porcelain: easy to shatter, terribly hard to mend.
To sum up: rather than respond passively after public opinion boils over, better to invite the parents to the table when the decision is first made. Public trust, after all, is the one thing that cannot be "pre-made".

tips.title: ⚠️ Kill the imported scaffolding

tips.text: The rebuttal rhythm: 您说得有道理，但是… / 这恰恰说明… — agree with a sliver, pivot on 但是/恰恰, strike with your point. Speed comes from the fixed frames.

phrases.text: 您说得有道理，但是问题没这么简单。
phrases.translation: Nín shuō de yǒu dàolǐ, dànshì wèntí méi zhème jiǎndān. — Fair point, but it's not that simple.

phrases.text: 这恰恰说明了我们的观点。
phrases.translation: Zhè qiàqià shuōmíng le wǒmen de guāndiǎn. — This proves precisely our point.

phrases.text: 对方辩友忽略了一个关键事实。
phrases.translation: Duìfāng biànyǒu hūlüè le yí ge guānjiàn shìshí. — Our opponents have overlooked a key fact.

phrases.text: 退一步说，即使如此，结论也不成立。
phrases.translation: Tuìyíbùshuō, jíshǐ rúcǐ, jiélùn yě bù chénglì. — Even granting that, the conclusion still fails.

phrases.text: 归根结底，这是个选择问题，而非技术问题。
phrases.translation: Guī gēn jié dǐ, zhè shì ge xuǎnzé wèntí, ér fēi jìshù wèntí. — Ultimately this is a question of choice, not of technology.

quizzes.title: Listening: 文化讲座

help.intro: A culture lecture that answers a question you've lived through this course: why hanzi survived. Full register: 非但…反而, 所谓, 乃在于.

tips.title: 非但…反而
tips.text: "Not only did it not…, on the contrary it…" — the strongest reversal frame in the language: 非但没有埋葬汉字，反而给了它新生.

quizzes.passageTitle: 讲座：汉字为什么没有消失
quizzes.passage:
各位好。今天我们谈一个问题：汉字为什么没有消失？
一百年前，不少学者曾断言，汉字太难，必将被拼音文字取代。在打字机时代，这种担忧看似有理：西文打字机噼啪作响，汉字却连一台像样的打字机都造不出来。
然而，历史开了一个玩笑。计算机的出现，非但没有埋葬汉字，反而给了它新生：今天，输入汉字的速度丝毫不逊于任何拼音文字。所谓"汉字危机"，就这样烟消云散了。
更耐人寻味的是，正是最古老的特性救了汉字——它记录的是意义，而不仅仅是声音。正因如此，上海人和广州人口音天差地别，写下来却是同一行字；我们今天读两千年前的文章，居然还能会心一笑。
归根结底，汉字的生命力，乃在于它把整个文明装进了方寸之间。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Lecture: why did Chinese characters not disappear?
Greetings. Today's question: why didn't Chinese characters die out?
A century ago, many scholars declared characters too difficult — surely to be replaced by alphabetic writing. In the typewriter age the worry seemed reasonable: Western typewriters clattered away, while no decent Chinese typewriter could even be built.
History, however, played a joke. The computer, far from burying the characters, gave them new life: typing Chinese today is every bit as fast as typing any alphabet. The so-called "character crisis" vanished like smoke.
More thought-provoking still: it was the most ancient property that saved them — characters record meaning, not merely sound. That is why a Shanghainese and a Cantonese, whose accents differ like heaven and earth, write the very same line; and why we can read essays from two thousand years ago and still smile in recognition.
In the end, the vitality of the characters lies precisely in this: they pack an entire civilization into a square inch.

options: 汉字会被拼音文字取代
questions.questionTranslation: What did scholars worry about a century ago?

questions.question: 什么给了汉字新生？
questions.questionTranslation: What gave the characters new life?

quizzes.title: Reading: 分析一篇短篇小说

help.intro: A complete flash story plus a critic's note — fiction and analysis in one sitting. Watch how the commentary reads meaning the story never states.

tips.title: 留白 — the unpainted space
tips.text: From ink painting: what's left blank carries the feeling. The critic's 不写一个"惨"字，而失落自现 is the C2 reading skill — hearing what the text declines to say.

quizzes.passage:
【微型小说：修表匠】
老周修了四十年表。铺子小得转不开身，墙上却挂满了钟，每一只都走得分毫不差。
如今来修表的人少了。年轻人看时间用手机，"手表？那是装饰品。"
这天，一个姑娘拿来一只旧上海牌手表："我爷爷的。走不了了，师傅您看还有救吗？"
老周戴上放大镜，拆开表壳，看了很久。"零件早就不产了。"他说。姑娘的眼圈红了。
"不过，"老周从抽屉最里面摸出一个小铁盒，"我这儿还存着最后一套。"
表修好了。姑娘问多少钱，老周摆摆手："我只收修表的钱——零件不要钱。它等这只表，等了二十年了。"

【短评】
小说不足三百字，却写尽了一个时代。结尾一句是全篇之眼：等待的不是零件，而是老周自己——等一个还需要他的人。作者不写一个"惨"字，而失落自现；不写一个"暖"字，而温情自见。所谓留白，此之谓也。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
[Flash fiction: The Watch Mender]
Old Zhou has mended watches for forty years. His shop is too small to turn around in, yet the walls are covered with clocks, every one keeping perfect time.
Few come to mend watches now. The young check their phones: "A watch? That's jewellery."
One day a girl brings in an old Shanghai-brand watch: "My grandfather's. It's stopped — master, can it be saved?"
Old Zhou puts on his loupe, opens the case, looks a long while. "The parts went out of production years ago," he says. The girl's eyes redden.
"However —" Old Zhou reaches into the back of a drawer and brings out a small tin box, "I still keep one last set."
The watch is mended. The girl asks the price. Old Zhou waves a hand: "I charge only for the mending — the parts are free. They've been waiting for this watch for twenty years."

[Brief commentary]
In under three hundred characters, the story writes out an entire era. The final line is the eye of the piece: what waited was not the parts but Old Zhou himself — waiting for someone who still needed him. The author writes no word for "sad", yet the loss shows itself; no word for "warm", yet the tenderness appears. This is what is meant by leaving blank space.

questions.question: 姑娘拿来的是什么表？
options: 她爷爷的旧上海牌手表
questions.questionTranslation: What watch does the girl bring?

questions.question: 短评认为，"等了二十年"的其实是谁？
questions.questionTranslation: According to the commentary, who was really waiting twenty years?

questions.question: "留白"在这里指什么？
options: 不直说而让感情自己显现
questions.questionTranslation: What does "leaving blank space" mean here?

quizzes.title: Reading: capstone — 一篇长篇特稿

help.intro: The capstone read: a full-length feature in literary-journalistic style. No questions about grammar now — only about meaning, structure and what's left unsaid.

tips.title: Read it twice
tips.text: Once for the man, once for the craft: the numbers doing emotional work (两分钱, 三十六块), the refrain 可他还在游, and an ending that answers the question without answering it.

quizzes.passage:
凌晨四点半，五十八岁的陈建国站在江边，把毛巾叠好，放进塑料袋。江水是黑的，只有对岸的灯，在水面上拉出几道细长的金线。
他游这条江，游了四十年。
一九八五年，他第一次横渡，是为了省两分钱的轮渡钱。那时他在对岸的纺织厂上班，一个月工资三十六块。"游过去，一个月能省下一块二，够给我娘买两斤猪肉。"
后来工厂倒了，轮渡停了，江上架起了三座大桥。地铁从江底穿过，八分钟一班。谁还需要游过去呢？
可他还在游。
"有人问我，桥都修好了，你游它干什么？"陈建国笑了，"我说，你们坐地铁，是为了到对岸去。我下水，不是为了对岸。"
医生说他的心脏比四十岁的人还好。老伴儿说他犟。儿子在深圳，视频里劝了十年："爸，危险。"他嘴上答应着，第二天四点半，闹钟一响，又拎起了塑料袋。
这些年，江水见过他结婚，见过他下岗，见过他送走母亲。水凉的时候，他知道秋天到了；水里漂着柳絮，他知道又是一年春天。"这条江认识我，"他说这话的时候，天边刚刚发白，"它比谁都清楚，我这一辈子，没偷过懒。"
五点整，他下水了。黑色的江面安静地裂开一道口子，又慢慢合上。对岸的灯一盏一盏地熄灭，城市醒了。
quizzes.passageTranslation:
Feature: The Crosser
At half past four in the morning, 58-year-old Chen Jianguo stands at the river's edge, folds his towel and puts it in a plastic bag. The water is black; only the lights of the far bank pull thin gold threads across the surface.
He has swum this river for forty years.
His first crossing, in 1985, was to save the two-cent ferry fare. He worked then in the textile mill on the far side, at 36 yuan a month. "Swimming across saved one yuan twenty a month — enough to buy my mother two catties of pork."
Later the mill closed, the ferry stopped, three great bridges rose over the river. The metro runs beneath it, every eight minutes. Who still needs to swim across?
Yet he still swims.
"People ask me — the bridges are built, what do you swim for?" Chen laughs. "I tell them: you ride the metro to reach the far bank. I don't get in the water for the far bank."
The doctor says his heart is younger than a forty-year-old's. His wife says he's stubborn. His son in Shenzhen has spent ten years urging over video calls: "Dad, it's dangerous." He agrees out loud — and the next morning at 4:30, when the alarm rings, picks up the plastic bag again.
Over the years the river has seen him marry, seen him laid off, seen him bury his mother. When the water turns cold he knows autumn has come; when willow catkins drift on it, another spring. "This river knows me," he says, as the horizon just begins to pale. "It knows better than anyone that in this life of mine, I never once slacked."
At five sharp he enters the water. The black surface quietly splits open a seam, then slowly closes. On the far bank the lights go out one by one. The city wakes.

questions.question: 陈建国一九八五年为什么横渡？
questions.questionTranslation: Why did Chen first swim across in 1985?

questions.question: "我下水，不是为了对岸"是什么意思？
options: 游泳本身就是他生活的意义
questions.questionTranslation: What does "I don't get in the water for the far bank" mean?

questions.question: 文章的结尾写城市醒了，有什么作用？
options: 把一个人的坚持放回大时代的背景里
questions.questionTranslation: What does the closing image of the waking city do?

tips.title: You've built the whole ladder
tips.text: Tones → 是 → 了 → 把 → 书面语 → irony. This speech uses all of it. Record yourself, compare with the model, and notice how far 从"你好"到这里 you've come.

phrases.text: 如果有人问我，学中文最难的是什么，我不会说是声调，也不会说是汉字。
phrases.translation: Rúguǒ yǒu rén wèn wǒ, xué Zhōngwén zuì nán de shì shénme… — If someone asks me what's hardest about learning Chinese…

phrases.text: 最难的，是敢于开口——从"你好"开始。
phrases.translation: Zuì nán de, shì gǎnyú kāikǒu — cóng nǐ hǎo kāishǐ. — The hardest is daring to speak — starting from "nǐ hǎo".

phrases.text: 语言不是知识，而是一条要游过去的江。
phrases.translation: Yǔyán bú shì zhīshi, ér shì yì tiáo yào yóu guòqù de jiāng. — A language is not knowledge but a river to be swum.

phrases.text: 桥再多，也代替不了自己下水。
phrases.translation: Qiáo zài duō, yě dài tì bù liǎo zìjǐ xià shuǐ. — However many the bridges, they can't replace entering the water yourself.

phrases.text: 所谓精通，不过是每天都愿意再下一次水而已。
phrases.translation: Suǒwèi jīngtōng, búguò shì měitiān dōu yuànyì zài xià yí cì shuǐ éryǐ. — So-called mastery is merely being willing to enter the water again, every day.
